name: Data from Local System
description:
Adversaries may search local system sources, such as file systems or local databases, to find files of interest and sensitive data prior to exfiltration.  

 

Access to local system data, which includes information stored by the operating system, often requires escalated privileges. Examples of local system data include authentication tokens, the device keyboard cache, Wi-Fi passwords, and photos. On Android, adversaries may also attempt to access files from external storage which may require additional storage-related permissions.

telemetry.name: Application Permission
telemetry.description: Declared or granted permissions of a mobile application.
telemetry.collection_focus: Compare manifest declarations with runtime granted state using authorized package inspection and own-app permission checks.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.

configuration_example.label: Inspect the owned Android lab application
configuration_example.note: Read-only snapshot on a consented debug device. Replace the example package with your owned test app. Output and access vary by Android build; this is not a permission-request event stream.

telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: File Access
telemetry.description: Access to file objects with user, process and access-right context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit File System plus a narrow SACL on a lab directory; on Linux select path/syscall rules and join associated Audit records.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

telemetry.name: OS API Execution
telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

strategies.name: Detection of Data from Local System

analytics.name: Analytic 1840
analytics.guidance: The defender correlates newly granted or recently exercised storage- or privilege-relevant access with burst reads of local files, local databases, or protected records from operating-system or external-storage locations, especially when the reads are inconsistent with app role, occur in background or locked-device context, or are followed by temporary data staging or network transmission. The analytic emphasizes Android-specific observables such as external storage access, app-private database reads where visible to the sensor, and repeated enumeration/read activity against local paths associated with media, tokens, caches, or exported application data.

tuning.description: Correlation window between permission state, local data reads, optional staging, and outbound transfer
Apps legitimately expected to read local files or databases such as backup, sync, file manager, security, or media management apps
Expected local paths, storage roots, and database locations for legitimate app behavior
Whether sensitive local data access should happen only during active user-driven workflows
Minimum number of file or record reads within a short interval required to indicate suspicious collection
Environment-specific list of high-value local paths such as external media roots, app export folders, token stores, or browser data locations
Minimum upload size expected if collection is followed by exfiltration

log_sources.name: android:MDMLog
log_sources.channel: Managed app granted or retaining storage-related or elevated access inconsistent with declared function prior to local data access activity

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Application queries or opens multiple local SQLite or app-associated database stores containing records unrelated to the app's declared function during the collection phase

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Application performs burst reads across local system paths, external storage, media directories, cache locations, or local database files within a short interval as the primary collection phase

analytics.name: Analytic 1841
analytics.guidance: The defender correlates supervised-device app posture and lifecycle context with repeated local file or local-database access effects, especially when a managed app reads browser, messaging, keychain-adjacent, or application-container data outside its expected role and then stages or uploads the result. Because direct low-level local system access visibility is weaker on iOS, the primary analytic is effect-based: managed app identity, file/database access where visible to the mobile sensor, background execution context, and near-term outbound communication.

tuning.description: Correlation window between managed app posture, local access activity, optional staging, and upload
Managed apps expected to access local records such as enterprise sync, backup, or approved investigation tools
Expected app-container or local artifact locations for legitimate workflows
Whether local record access should happen only during active user interaction
Minimum number of local file or record reads in a short interval required for alerting
Environment-specific list of high-value browser, messaging, token, or local record artifacts
Minimum outbound volume consistent with recent local data collection

log_sources.name: iOS:MDMLog
log_sources.channel: Supervised managed app without expected local export, sync, or forensic role accesses or stages local records inconsistent with policy baseline

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Application performs repeated record access, container traversal, or local data extraction processing against local stores before staging or transmission

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Application reads multiple local container files, browser-history artifacts, messaging artifacts, or local records in rapid sequence during the collection phase
